a1.say: Let's solve Consistent Hashing Ring, using the Sorted Ring plus Binary Search approach.

a1.cap: Spread keys across cache servers so adding or removing a server moves few keys. Positions on a ring of 360 slots come from h(s) = Σ (i + 1) · code(s[i]) mod 360 (character codes, i from 0). Implement HashRing() with addNode(name), removeNode(name) and getNode(key): the owner is the first node at or clockwise after h(key), wrapping around. Node positions never collide in the tests, and getNode is only called when a node exists.

Implement Hash Ring with add Node(name), remove Node(name) and get Node(key): the owner is the first node at or clockwise after h of key, wrapping around. Node positions never collide in the tests, and get Node is only called when a node exists.

a1.cap: Keep the node positions sorted. To place a key, binary search for the first node position at or after the key's hash; if none, wrap around to the first node.
Removing a node only moves the keys it owned to its clockwise neighbour, unlike hash mod N which reshuffles almost everything. Real systems add many virtual nodes per server to balance load.

Let's walk through it with the calls HashRing(), addNode("alpha"), addNode("beta"), addNode("gamma"), getNode("user:42"), getNode("img:3"), getNode("cart:9"), removeNode("beta"), getNode("user:42"), addNode("delta"), getNode("alpha"), getNode("user:7").
a1.say: Let's walk through it with the calls Hash Ring, add Node("alpha"), add Node("beta"), add Node("gamma"), get Node("user:42"), get Node("img:3"), get Node("cart:9"), remove Node("beta"), get Node("user:42"), add Node("delta"), get Node("alpha"), get Node("user:7").

a1.cap: Node 'alpha' sits at position 110 on the ring.
Node 'beta' sits at position 316 on the ring.
Node 'gamma' sits at position 105 on the ring.
Key 'user:42' hashes to 258; the next node clockwise is 'beta'.
Key 'img:3' hashes to 39; the next node clockwise is 'gamma'.
Key 'cart:9' hashes to 291; the next node clockwise is 'beta'.
Node 'beta' leaves. Its keys move to the next node clockwise.
Key 'user:42' hashes to 258; the next node clockwise is 'gamma'.
Node 'delta' sits at position 135 on the ring.
Key 'alpha' hashes to 110; the next node clockwise is 'alpha'.
Key 'user:7' hashes to 286; the next node clockwise is 'gamma'.
Time complexity is O(log n) lookup and extra space is O(n).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of log n lookup and extra space is O of n.
